                Taking complements, we get 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i}) 
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i+1})
                        + O(\gamma)\,.

                This contradicts \cref{eq:main:constRegGuarantee} (at the $i$-th step) since $H_{i+1}$ is feasible for the $i$-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM{} constructed by \cref{alg:main} and, hence, $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i+1})\geq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(i)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement:
The only computationally non-trivial step in \cref{alg:main} is the call to boosted constraint regression and the construction of and sampling from distributions $\customcal{D}_i$ and $\customcal{P}^\star_i$ via rejection sampling.
            Since the assumptions of \cref{thm:sampleComplexity} hold (see \cref{lem:main:assumptions}), it promises that the call to boosted constraint regression is efficient and runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$. 
            Hence, it remains to bound the time of rejection sampling.
            
            For this, it suffices to show a lower bound on the mass of $\customcal{D}(S_i)$ and $\customcal{P}^\star(S_i)$ for each $i$ so that it is not too small, since the inverse of this quantity is the expected number of samples from $\customcal{D}$ and $\customcal{P}^\star$ one would need to see a single sample in $S_i$. 
            We already proved this in \cref{eq:main:massGuarantee}. 
            In particular, the bounds in \cref{eq:main:massGuarantee} ensure that each call to the sampling oracle in \cref{alg:main}, with probability $1-\eta$, runs in time $O((\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})\log{\nfrac{1}{\eta}})$ (for any $\eta\in(0,1)$). 
            Selecting $\eta$ to be a suitably small multiple of $\delta$ and taking a union bound over $\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$ calls implies the claim with only a logarithmic increase in the running time.

nodes.statement_short: Each regression call is polynomial; rejection sampling is fast because surviving sets keep constant mass.

nodes.name: Rescale parameters
nodes.statement:
We use the algorithm in \cref{alg:main}.
        First, we rescale $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$ to ensure that $\varepsilon\leq \nfrac{\alpha}{6}$ and $\delta\leq \sigma^2\varepsilon^{2q}$. 
        Due to the scaling in $\varepsilon$, the relation between $\zeta$ and $\varepsilon$ becomes $\zeta\leq O\binparen{(\sigma\varepsilon)^{5q^2}\alpha^{8q}}$ where $\varepsilon$ is the rescaled accuracy parameter, and we will use this updated relation in our analysis.
        Due to the scaling in $\delta$, the running time increases by logarithmic factors in $\max\inbrace{\nfrac{1}{\sigma},\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon^q}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 and its proof
nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Assumptions Required by \cref{thm:constReg} Hold.}
            We begin by proving that the assumptions required by \cref{thm:constReg} hold in each iteration where the for-loop executes.
            \begin{lemma} In each iteration $i$ where the for-loop in \cref{alg:main} executes, the following hold:
                \begin{enumerate}
                    \item Degree-$k$ polynomials $(\nfrac{\zeta}{\gamma})$-approximate $\hypo{H}$ with respect to  $\customcal{D}_i$ in $L_1$-norm. 
                    \item $(\customcal{D}^\star_i,\customcal{P}^\star_i,\customcal{D})$ is a valid PIU learning instance with constants $\sigma'\geq \nfrac{\alpha^2 \sigma}{3}$ and $q'=q$.
                \end{enumerate}
            \end{lemma}
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:main:assumptions}]
                Due to the guarantee of \cref{thm:constReg}, each of $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$ is a degree-$k$ PTF over $d$ variables.
                Since $S_i$ is an intersection of at most $T=\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ sets from $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$, $S_i$ belongs to the family of the intersections of (at most) $\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ degree-$k$ PTFs over $d$-variables, which has a VC dimension at most $\wt{O}(d^k/\gamma)$.
                Now, since the for-loop executes in the $i$-th iteration, the check in Step~\ref{step:alg:main:massCheck} ensures that with probability $1-\delta$, 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(S_i)\geq \Omega({\gamma})
                    \quadtext{and}
                    \customcal{P}^\star(S_i)\geq \frac{\alpha}{2}-\gamma \geq \frac{\alpha}{3}\,,
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                due to uniform convergence over the class of (at most) $\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ degree-$k$ PTFs over $d$-variables and $\gamma\leq \varepsilon \leq \nfrac{\alpha}{6}$.
                Further, since degree-$k$ polynomials $\zeta$-approximate $\hypo{H}$ with respect to  $\customcal{D}$ in $L_1$-norm, for every $H'\in \hypo{H}$, there is a degree-$k$ polynomial $p'\colon \mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ such that 
                \[
                    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\customcal{D}}\insquare{\abs{p'(x) - \mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in H'}}}\leq \zeta\,.
                \]
                Since $\customcal{D}(S_i)\geq \Omega(\gamma)$ and $\customcal{D}_i$ is the truncation of $\customcal{D}$ to $S_i$, a change of measure, implies 
                \[
                    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\customcal{D}_i}\insquare{\abs{p'(x) - \mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in H'}}}\leq O\inparen{\frac{\zeta}{\gamma}}\,.
                \]
                Since this holds for each $H'\in \hypo{H}$, the first result follows.

                To prove the second claim, it suffices to show that $\customcal{P}^\star_i$ is the truncation of $\customcal{D}^\star_i$ to the set ${H^\star}$ (which holds by construction) and that $\customcal{D}_i$ and $\customcal{D}^\star_i$ satisfy \cref{asmp:smoothness} with the specified constants.
                To prove the latter, consider any measurable set $T\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.
                Observe that due to \cref{asmp:smoothness}
                \[
                    \customcal{D}^\star_i(T)
                    = \frac{\customcal{D}^\star(T\cap S_i)}{\customcal{D}^\star(S_i)}
                    \leq \frac{\customcal{D}(T\cap S_i)^{1/q}}{\sigma\cdot \customcal{D}^\star(S_i)}
                    \leq \frac{3\cdot \customcal{D}(T\cap S_i)^{1/q}}{\sigma \alpha^2}
                    \,.
                \]
                Where in the last inequality we used \cref{eq:main:massGuarantee} and the fact that $\customcal{D}^\star(S_i)\geq \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\customcal{P}^\star(S_i)\geq \alpha\customcal{P}^\star(S_i)$ (due to \cref{asmp:posFraction}).
                We can continue the above chain of inequalities as follows 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}^\star_i(T)
                    \leq \frac{3}{\sigma\alpha^2} \cdot 
                        \inparen{\frac{\customcal{D}(T\cap S_i)}{\customcal{D}(S_i)}}^{1/q}
                    = \frac{3}{\sigma\alpha^2}\cdot \customcal{D}_i(T)^{1/q}\,.
                \]
            \end{proof}

nodes.name: Two cases
nodes.section: 4.2 Proof of 3.3 (Computationally Efficient Algorithm)

nodes.name: Case A: loop breaks
nodes.statement:
\itparagraph{Case A (For-loop breaks at iteration $i$):}
            First, suppose that the if statement first broke at step $i$, then the check in Step~\ref{step:alg:main:massCheck} (along with uniform convergence; as discussed in \cref{lem:main:assumptions}) implies that $\customcal{D}(S_i)=\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap\dots H_{i-1})\leq O(\gamma)$ and $H=H_1\cap H_2\cap\dots H_{i-1}$.
            Therefore, $\customcal{D}(H\setminus {H^\star})\leq \customcal{D}(H)\leq O(\gamma)$. 
            Applying \cref{asmp:smoothness} yields $\customcal{D}^\star(H \setminus {H^\star}) \leq \sigma^{-1}\cdot \gamma^{1/q}\leq \varepsilon$.
            Further, since all previous iterations $1,2,\dots,i-1$, the for-loop executed, \cref{eq:main:constRegGuarantee} holds and implies that 
            $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H_i)\leq (i-1)\gamma^2\leq \gamma\leq \varepsilon$ where we used that $i\leq T=\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$.
            Combining these bounds implies that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\triangle H)\leq 2\varepsilon\,,
            \]
            completing the proof of correctness in this case.

nodes.name: Case B: loop never breaks
nodes.statement:
\itparagraph{Case B (For-loop never breaks):}
            Now, we consider the other case, where the break condition is never satisfied and, hence, all $T$ iterations of the for loop take place.
            \begin{align*}
                \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H)~~
                &\leq~~ \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{{H^\star}\cap H_1 \cap H_2 \cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_i}\\
                &\leq~~ \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{{H^\star}\setminus H_i}\\
                &\Stackrel{\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:main:constRegGuarantee}}}}{\leq}~~ 
                    \gamma\,. 
                    \tagnum{since $T=\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$}{eq:computational:caseB}
            \end{align*}
            To finish the proof of correctness in Case B, we need to bound $\customcal{D}^\star(H \setminus {H^\star})$. 
            For this, we will use the following claim to bound $\customcal{D}(H \setminus {H^\star})$, and then apply \cref{asmp:smoothness}.
            \begin{claim} It holds that 
                \begin{align*}
                    \customcal{D}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_1)
                    &\geq \customcal{D}(H_1\setminus H_2) - \gamma^2\\
                    &\geq \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\setminus H_3) - 2\gamma^2\\
                    &~~\vdots\\
                    &\geq \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots H_{T-1}\setminus H_T) - (T-1)\gamma^2\,.
                \end{align*}
            \end{claim}
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:main:chaining}]
                Toward a contradiction, suppose that for some index $i$
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_i\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_{i}) + \gamma^2\,.
                \]
                Replacing the intersection on the LHS from $H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_i$ to $H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}$, implies
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_{i}) + \gamma^2\,.
                \]
                Equivalently, 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i}) 
                        + \frac{\gamma^2}{\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1})}\,.
                \]
                Since $\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1})\geq \Omega(\gamma)$ due to \cref{lem:main:assumptions}, the above implies that 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i}) 
                        + O(\gamma)\,.
                \]
                Taking complements, we get 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i}) 
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i+1})
                        + O(\gamma)\,.
                \]
                This contradicts \cref{eq:main:constRegGuarantee} (at the $i$-th step) since $H_{i+1}$ is feasible for the $i$-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM{} constructed by \cref{alg:main} and, hence, $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i+1})\geq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(i)$.
            \end{proof}
            Now we will use \cref{lem:main:chaining} to bound $\customcal{D}(H\setminus{H^\star})$. 
            Since the sets $\inbrace{H_1\cap H_2\cap\dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_i}_i$ are disjoint, it follows that 
            \[
                T\cdot \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1} \setminus H_T)
                - T(T-1)\gamma^2
                \leq \sum_i \customcal{D}(H_1 \cap H_2 \cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_i)
                \leq 1\,.
            \]
            Therefore, 
            \begin{align*}
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus H_T)
                \leq \frac{1}{T} + (T-1)\gamma^2
                \leq 2\gamma\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*}
            Apart from this, as $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}(H_T)\leq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(T)+\gamma^2$ and ${H^\star}$ is feasible for the $T$-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM{} (so $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}({H^\star})\geq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(T)$), the following also holds
            \[
                \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}(H_T)
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}({H^\star})
                + \gamma^2\,.
            \]
            and consequently, 
            \[
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus {H^\star})
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus H_T)
                + \gamma^2\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            Hence,
            \[
                \customcal{D}(H \setminus {H^\star})
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus {H^\star})
                ~~~\Stackrel{\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:main:chainingGuarantee}}},~\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:main:optimalityGuaranteeTth}}}}{\leq}~~~  
                \gamma^2 + 2\gamma
                \leq 3\gamma\,.
            \]
        Applying \cref{asmp:smoothness}, we have $\customcal{D}^\star(H \setminus {H^\star}) \leq \sigma^{-1} \cdot \customcal{D}(H \setminus {H^\star})^{1/q} \leq \sigma^{-1} \cdot (3\gamma)^{1/q}\leq 3\varepsilon$. 
        Combining this with \textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:computational:caseB}}} implies that 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\triangle H)\leq 2\varepsilon\,,
        \]
        completing the proof of correctness in Case B.

nodes.name: H* feasible for the last instance
nodes.statement:
Apart from this, as $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}(H_T)\leq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(T)+\gamma^2$ and ${H^\star}$ is feasible for the $T$-th instance of Pessimistic-ERM{} (so $\customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}({H^\star})\geq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM}(T)$), the following also holds
            \[
                \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}(H_T)
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}}({H^\star})
                + \gamma^2\,.
            \]
            and consequently, 
            \[
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus {H^\star})
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus H_T)
                + \gamma^2\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]

nodes.name: D(H minus H*) at most 3 gamma
nodes.statement:
Hence,
            \[
                \customcal{D}(H \setminus {H^\star})
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{T-1}\setminus {H^\star})
                ~~~\Stackrel{\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:main:chainingGuarantee}}},~\textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:main:optimalityGuaranteeTth}}}}{\leq}~~~  
                \gamma^2 + 2\gamma
                \leq 3\gamma\,.
            \]

nodes.name: Smoothness gives D* error 2 eps
nodes.statement:
Applying \cref{asmp:smoothness}, we have $\customcal{D}^\star(H \setminus {H^\star}) \leq \sigma^{-1} \cdot \customcal{D}(H \setminus {H^\star})^{1/q} \leq \sigma^{-1} \cdot (3\gamma)^{1/q}\leq 3\varepsilon$. 
        Combining this with \textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:computational:caseB}}} implies that 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\triangle H)\leq 2\varepsilon\,,
        \]
        completing the proof of correctness in Case B.

nodes.name: Running time via Lemma 4.6
nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Computational Efficiency.}
        Finally, it remains to show that \cref{alg:main} runs in sample polynomial time.
        
        \begin{lemma} Consider the setting of \cref{thm:main}. \cref{alg:main} runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ with probability $1-\delta$ where $n=\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$.
        \end{lemma}
        \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:main:rejectionSampling}]
            The only computationally non-trivial step in \cref{alg:main} is the call to boosted constraint regression and the construction of and sampling from distributions $\customcal{D}_i$ and $\customcal{P}^\star_i$ via rejection sampling.
            Since the assumptions of \cref{thm:sampleComplexity} hold (see \cref{lem:main:assumptions}), it promises that the call to boosted constraint regression is efficient and runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$. 
            Hence, it remains to bound the time of rejection sampling.
            
            For this, it suffices to show a lower bound on the mass of $\customcal{D}(S_i)$ and $\customcal{P}^\star(S_i)$ for each $i$ so that it is not too small, since the inverse of this quantity is the expected number of samples from $\customcal{D}$ and $\customcal{P}^\star$ one would need to see a single sample in $S_i$. 
            We already proved this in \cref{eq:main:massGuarantee}. 
            In particular, the bounds in \cref{eq:main:massGuarantee} ensure that each call to the sampling oracle in \cref{alg:main}, with probability $1-\eta$, runs in time $O((\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})\log{\nfrac{1}{\eta}})$ (for any $\eta\in(0,1)$). 
            Selecting $\eta$ to be a suitably small multiple of $\delta$ and taking a union bound over $\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$ calls implies the claim with only a logarithmic increase in the running time.

        \end{proof}

nodes.name: S_i is an intersection of PTFs
nodes.statement:
Due to the guarantee of \cref{thm:constReg}, each of $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$ is a degree-$k$ PTF over $d$ variables.
                Since $S_i$ is an intersection of at most $T=\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ sets from $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$, $S_i$ belongs to the family of the intersections of (at most) $\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ degree-$k$ PTFs over $d$-variables, which has a VC dimension at most $\wt{O}(d^k/\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Mass guarantee for S_i
nodes.statement:
Now, since the for-loop executes in the $i$-th iteration, the check in Step~\ref{step:alg:main:massCheck} ensures that with probability $1-\delta$, 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(S_i)\geq \Omega({\gamma})
                    \quadtext{and}
                    \customcal{P}^\star(S_i)\geq \frac{\alpha}{2}-\gamma \geq \frac{\alpha}{3}\,,
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                due to uniform convergence over the class of (at most) $\nfrac{1}{\gamma}$ degree-$k$ PTFs over $d$-variables and $\gamma\leq \varepsilon \leq \nfrac{\alpha}{6}$.
nodes.section: 4.2 Proof of 3.3 (Computationally Efficient Algorithm)

nodes.name: Change of measure keeps approximability
nodes.statement:
Further, since degree-$k$ polynomials $\zeta$-approximate $\hypo{H}$ with respect to  $\customcal{D}$ in $L_1$-norm, for every $H'\in \hypo{H}$, there is a degree-$k$ polynomial $p'\colon \mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ such that 
                \[
                    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\customcal{D}}\insquare{\abs{p'(x) - \mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in H'}}}\leq \zeta\,.
                \]
                Since $\customcal{D}(S_i)\geq \Omega(\gamma)$ and $\customcal{D}_i$ is the truncation of $\customcal{D}$ to $S_i$, a change of measure, implies 
                \[
                    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{\customcal{D}_i}\insquare{\abs{p'(x) - \mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in H'}}}\leq O\inparen{\frac{\zeta}{\gamma}}\,.
                \]
                Since this holds for each $H'\in \hypo{H}$, the first result follows.

nodes.statement: To prove the second claim, it suffices to show that $\customcal{P}^\star_i$ is the truncation of $\customcal{D}^\star_i$ to the set ${H^\star}$ (which holds by construction) and that $\customcal{D}_i$ and $\customcal{D}^\star_i$ satisfy \cref{asmp:smoothness} with the specified constants.

nodes.statement:

                \[

nodes.name: Rewrite in conditional form
nodes.statement:
Replacing the intersection on the LHS from $H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_i$ to $H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}$, implies
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}\setminus H_{i}) + \gamma^2\,.
                \]
                Equivalently, 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i}) 
                        + \frac{\gamma^2}{\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1})}\,.
                \]

nodes.name: Use the mass guarantee of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement:
Since $\customcal{D}(H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1})\geq \Omega(\gamma)$ due to \cref{lem:main:assumptions}, the above implies that 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i+1})
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(\mathbb{R}^d\setminus H_{i}) 
                        + O(\gamma)\,.
                \]
                Taking complements, we get 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i}) 
                    > \customcal{D}_{H_1\cap H_2\cap \dots \cap H_{i-1}}(H_{i+1})
                        + O(\gamma)\,.
                \]

Condition on all of the above events happening. 
                Fix any $1\leq i\leq T$ and $\gamma=\sqrt{\nfrac{2}{(\alpha\sigma)} }\cdot \zeta^{1/(4q)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of (R3)
nodes.statement:
Recall the definition of $H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}$ from \cref{eq:constReg:optimalSolution} and that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}_{\rm PERM} = \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})$ (from \cref{eq:constReg:expectedValue:defOPT}).
            We divide the proof of \cref{result:constReg:optimality} into two parts.
            The first part shows that the \textit{expectation} of the objective value attained by each hypothesis $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$ from \cref{alg:constReg} is close to $\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})$ (\cref{lem:constReg:expectedValue}).
            
            The second part shows that the selected $H$ has an objective value close to $\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})$ with high probability (\cref{lem:constReg:boost}).

            

        \paragraph{Part 1 (Expected Value of Optimal).}
            \begin{restatable}[Expected Value of Optimal]{lemma}{constrainedRegExpValue} For each $1\leq i\leq T$, $H_i$ satisfies
                \[
                    \operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{U_i\sim \customcal{D}}\insquare{
                        \frac{\abs{H_i\cap U_i}}{\abs{U_i}} 
                    }
                    \leq 
                    \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})
                    + O\inparen{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\alpha\sigma}}} \cdot \zeta^{1/(4q)}
                    + O(\delta)
                    \,. 
                \]
            \end{restatable}   

            \paragraph{Outline of the Proof of \cref{lem:constReg:expectedValue} (\cref{sec:proofof:lem:constReg:expectedValue}).}
            Next, we briefly outline the proof of \cref{lem:constReg:expectedValue} and present the complete proof in the next section (\cref{sec:proofof:lem:constReg:expectedValue}).
            This proof is the part of our analysis that is inspired by the analysis of \textsf{L1-Regression}{} by \citet*{kalai2008agnostically}.
            The proof of \cref{lem:constReg:expectedValue} follows the ideas in the analysis of \textsf{L1-Regression}{}, but needs to account for some technicalities:
            First, unlike \textsf{L1-Regression}{} which selects the best threshold in $[0,1]$ (\cref{alg:l1reg}), \cref{alg:constReg} has to select a threshold bounded away from 1 to ensure that the output hypothesis will be feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} (which is required to establish \cref{result:constReg:feasibility} and, in particular, to prove \cref{lem:constReg:feasibility:unconditional}).
            In the proof, we observe that this only changes the expected value by a small amount.
            Second, the analysis of \textsf{L1-Regression}{} relies on the polynomial $p_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}$ (which approximates $H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}$) being feasible for the corresponding optimization problem.
            For \textsf{L1-Regression}{}, this always holds since the optimization problem solved by \textsf{L1-Regression}{} is unconstrained (\cref{alg:l1reg}).
            For \cref{alg:constReg} this is not always the case.
            But, we show that $p_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}$ is feasible with high probability, and carry out our proof conditioned on this event.
            This conditioning does not skew the expectations significantly as the involved random variables are suitably bounded. 

        
        \paragraph{Part 2 (Boosting via Repetition).}
        Next, using a standard argument one can show that selecting the ``best performing'' hypothesis from $H_1,H_2,\dots,H_T$ (as evaluated on a fresh set of samples) has an objective value close to optimal with probability $1-\delta$.
        The proof of \cref{lem:constReg:boost} is standard and is provided in \cref{sec:proofof:lem:constReg:boost} for completeness.
        \begin{lemma}[Boosting via Repetition] The hypothesis $H$ output by \cref{alg:constReg}, with probability $1-\delta$, satisfies that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}(H)
                \leq 
                \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})
                +  
                O\inparen{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\alpha\sigma}}}
                \cdot \zeta^{1/(4q)}
                +
                    O(\delta)
                \,.
            \]
        \end{lemma}

nodes.section: 5.1 Learning with Smooth Positive Samples
nodes.statement_short: If D* is smooth w.r.t. a known samplable D, positive samples suffice to PAC learn H, efficiently under L1 approximability.
assumptions: feature distribution $\customcal{D}^\star$ that is $(\sigma,q)$-smooth (see \cref{asmp:smoothness}) with respect to a known reference $\customcal{D}$ that one can efficiently sample from
conclusions: $\wt{O}\inparen{{\varepsilon^{-2q}}\cdot \inparen{\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H}) + \log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}$ independent positive samples are sufficient to $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learn $\hypo{H}$ with respect to $\customcal{D}^\star$.
nodes.label: cor:smooth_classification

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.1

nodes.section: 5.1 Learning with Smooth Positive Samples
nodes.statement_short: The setting is the standard PIU model, so Theorems 1.1 and 3.3 apply.

nodes.name: PIU learning in the List Decoding PIU Model
nodes.statement:
Consider the List Decoding PIU Model (\cref{def:list}) and $\varepsilon,\delta\in (0,\nfrac{1}{2})$.
            \begin{itemize}
                \item[$\triangleright$] (Sample Complexity)~~ There is an algorithm that, given $\varepsilon$ and 
                $\widetilde{O}\binparen{\binparen{\ell\cdot \sinparen{\nfrac{\ell}{(\varepsilon\sigma)}}^{2q} + {\varepsilon^{-3}}}\cdot \sinparen{\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})} + \log \nfrac{1}{\delta}}}$ independent samples from $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star)$, outputs a hypothesis $\wh{h}$, such that, with probability $1-\delta$,
                \[
                    \Pr_{\customcal{D}^\star}\binparen{\wh{h}(x) \neq h^\star(x)} \leq \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                \item[$\triangleright$] (Computational Complexity)~~ 
                    Suppose $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star) \geq \alpha$. 
                    Let $k \geq 1$ be such that $\hypo{H}$ is $\zeta$-approximable by degree-$k$ polynomials in the $L_1$-norm with respect to $\customcal{D}_{i^\star}$ for the index $i^\star$ in \cref{def:list} and $\zeta\leq O\sinparen{{\alpha^3\sigma}{}}^{2q}\cdot \sinparen{\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}}^{1+4q}$.
                    There is a polynomial time algorithm that given $n=\mathrm{poly}(d^k, \nfrac{1}{\zeta}, \nfrac{\ell}{\varepsilon}, \log \nfrac{1}{\delta})$ samples from $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star)$ and $\customcal{D}_1,\customcal{D}_2,\dots,\customcal{D}_\ell$, outputs a hypothesis $\wh{h}$ such that, with probability $1-\delta$,
                    \[
                        \Pr_{\customcal{D}^\star}\binparen{\wh{h}(x) \neq h^\star(x)} \leq \varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    The algorithm runs in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time.
            \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 5.2 Learning with Positive Samples and Lists of Unlabeled Samples
nodes.statement_short: With a list of l unlabeled distributions one of which witnesses smoothness, H is learnable with poly samples, efficiently under L1 approximability.
assumptions: Consider the List Decoding PIU Model (\cref{def:list}) and $\varepsilon,\delta\in (0,\nfrac{1}{2})$.
conclusions: The algorithm runs in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time.
nodes.label: thm:listDecoding

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement:
First, we prove the computational complexity result. 
                The proof of the sample complexity result is analogous and is presented at the end.

                \paragraph{Computational Complexity.}
                    The algorithm in \cref{thm:main} is not directly applicable in the List Decoding PIU Model because we do not know the index $i^\star$ of the distribution that is ``close'' to $\customcal{D}^\star$.
                    However, the simple extension of the algorithm in \cref{thm:main} described in \cref{alg:listDecoding} works.
                    Since each call to \cref{alg:main} uses $n=\mathrm{poly}(d^k, \nfrac{1}{\zeta}, \nfrac{\ell}{\varepsilon}, \log \nfrac{1}{\delta})$  samples and runs in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time, the sample complexity and running time claimed in the theorem hold.
                    It remains to prove the correctness of \cref{alg:listDecoding}.
                    Toward this, we claim that, with probability $1-\delta$, the hypothesis $H^{(1)},H^{(2)},\dots,H^{(\ell)}$ satisfy the following properties.
                    \begin{enumerate}[label=(P\arabic*)]
                        \item For each $1\leq i\leq \ell$ that is included in the set $S$ satisfies, $\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{{H^\star}\setminus H^{(i)}}\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon\alpha}{\ell}$. \item $\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{{H^\star}\triangle H^{(i^\star)}}\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}$. \item $i^\star\in S$. \end{enumerate}
                    First, we complete the proof of correctness, assuming that the above claim is true.
                    Condition on the above event happening.
                    First, observe that 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star} \triangle \wh{H}}
                        = \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star} \triangle \bigcap\nolimits_{i\in S} H^{(i)}}
                        = 
                        \underbrace{\customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star} \setminus \bigcap\nolimits_{i\in S} H^{(i)}}}_{\text{Term 1: False-Negative Rate}}
                        + 
                       \underbrace{ \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{\bigcap\nolimits_{i\in S} H^{(i)} \setminus {H^\star}}}_{\text{Term 2: False-Positive Rate}}\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                    These terms can be bounded as follows
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star}~\setminus~ \bigcap\nolimits_{i\in S} H^{(i)}}
                     &=\sum_{i\in S} \customcal{D}^\star \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H^{(i)}}
                     ~~\Stackrel{{\rm \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1}}}{\leq}~~ \ell \cdot \frac{\varepsilon}{\ell}
                     = \varepsilon\,,
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \\
                     \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{\bigcap\nolimits_{i\in S} H^{(i)}~\setminus~{H^\star}}
                        &~~\Stackrel{\rm\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3}}{\leq}~~ \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{H^{(i^\star)}~\setminus~{H^\star}}
                        ~~\Stackrel{\rm\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}}{\leq}~~
                            \varepsilon\,.\addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*} 
                The result follows by rescaling $\varepsilon$ to $\nfrac{\varepsilon}{2}$.

                It remains to prove that Properties~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1}, \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}, and \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3} hold with probability $1-\delta$.
                Property~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2} follows immediately from \cref{thm:main} since the distribution $\customcal{D}_{i^\star}$ satisfies the conditions required by \cref{thm:main} by definition of the list decoding model.
                To prove Properties~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1} and \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3}, let $\hypo{P}_{\cap 1/\varepsilon}(k)$ denote the hypothesis class of intersections of $(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})$ degree-$k$ PTFs which has VC dimension $\wt{O}\sinparen{\nfrac{d^k}{\varepsilon}}$; hence, in particular, $O(\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell})$-uniform convergence holds with respect to the set of samples $P$ constructed in \cref{alg:listDecoding} and the class $\hypo{P}_{\cap 1/\varepsilon}(k)$.
                Moreover, by the construction in \cref{alg:main}, $H^{(1)},\dots,H^{(\ell)}\in \hypo{P}_{\cap 1/\varepsilon}(k)$. 
                Now, Property~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1} holds since, for each $i\in S$, we have $\nfrac{\abs{H^{(i)}\cap P}}{\abs{P}}\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon}{(2\ell)}$ which by $O(\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell})$-uniform convergence, implies that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star} \setminus H^{(i)})\leq \customcal{P}^\star({H^\star} \setminus H^{(i)})\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}$.
                Similarly, Property~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3} holds since, from Property~\cref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}, we know that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H^{(i^\star)})\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon\alpha}{\ell}$ and, as $\customcal{D}({H^\star})\geq \alpha$, it follows that $\customcal{P}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H^{(i^\star)})\leq \nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}$: furthermore, by $O(\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell})$-uniform convergence over $\customcal{P}^\star$, we have $\nfrac{\abs{H^{(i^\star)} \cap P}}{\abs{P}}\leq O(\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell})$.
                    

            \begin{algorithm}[ht!]
            \caption{Efficient Algorithm to Learn from Positive Samples and List of Unlabeled Samples} \begin{algorithmic}
                \Require $\varepsilon, \delta,  \alpha , q, \sigma, k, \ell$ 
                \Ensure Sample access to $\customcal{P}^\star=\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})$ and each of $\customcal{D}_1,\customcal{D}_2,\dots,\customcal{D}_\ell$
                \State Let $P$ be a set of $m=\wt{O}\inparen{\varepsilon^{-2}\cdot \inparen{\nfrac{\textrm{\rm VC}(\hypo{H})}{\varepsilon} + \log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}$ independent samples from $\customcal{P}^\star$
                \State Initialize $S$ as the empty set $\emptyset$
                \For{$1\leq i \leq \ell$}
                    \State Obtain $H^{(i)}$ from \cref{alg:main} with positive sample distribution $\customcal{P}^\star$ and (imperfect) 
                    \item[] \phantom{.}~~~~ unlabeled distribution $\customcal{D}_i$ and parameters: accuracy $\nfrac{\varepsilon}{\ell}$, confidence $\nfrac{\delta}{\ell}$, smoothness 
                    \item[] \phantom{.}~~~~  parameters $(\sigma,q)$, lower bound on mass $\alpha$, and number $k$
                    \vspace{2mm}
                    \State \textbf{If} $\sabs{H^{(i)}\cap P}\geq 1-\nfrac{\varepsilon}{(2\ell)}$, \textbf{then,} add index $i$ to $S$
                    \State \textit{$\#$~~~Guarantees:~~$H^{(i)}$ and $S$ satisfy Properties~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1}, \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}, and \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3} with probability $1-\delta$} 
                \EndFor
                \State \Return $\wh{H}\coloneqq \bigcap_{i\in S} H^{(i)}$
            \end{algorithmic}
            \end{algorithm}
 

                \paragraph{Sample Complexity.}
                For the sample complexity result, we use the variant of \cref{alg:listDecoding}, where each call to \cref{alg:main} is replaced by a call to \cref{alg:sampleComplexity}.
                Further, the set of samples $P$ is only of size $\wt{O}\inparen{\varepsilon^{-2}\cdot \inparen{\nfrac{\textrm{\rm VC}(\hypo{H})}{\varepsilon} + \log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}$.
                The claimed sample complexity follows from the sample complexity guarantee of \cref{alg:sampleComplexity} in \cref{thm:sampleComplexity} and the specified size of $P$.
                It remains to prove correctness.
                If Properties~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1}, \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}, and \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3}  hold, then correctness follows from \cref{eq:listDecoding:1,eq:listDecoding:2,eq:listDecoding:3}.
                So it suffices to prove that Properties~\ref{property:listDecoding:proof:1}, \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:2}, and \ref{property:listDecoding:proof:3}  hold with probability $1-\delta$.
                This proof is identical to the one presented above for computational complexity except that the class $\hypo{P}_{\cap1/\varepsilon}(k)$ is replaced by $\hypo{H}$ and noting that that this improves the factor of $\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{P}_{\cap1/\varepsilon}(k))=\wt{O}(\nfrac{d^k}{\varepsilon})$ to $\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H})$.

nodes.name: Exponential family with polynomial sufficient statistics
nodes.statement:
The unlabeled distribution comes from an exponential family with polynomial sufficient statistics, which is a parametric family of the form
    \[ \customcal{E}(x; \theta) \propto h(x) \cdot e^{ \inangle{\theta, t(x)}}\,, \]
    where $t(x)$ is an $m$-dimensional vector whose components are polynomials in $x$.

nodes.name: Natural parameter space
nodes.statement: The set of parameters $\theta$ for which the density of $\customcal{E}(\theta)$ is well defined is called the \textit{natural parameter space} $\overline{\Theta}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Truncated Estimation with Unknown Survival Set
also_stated_at: The set of $\theta$ for which the density of $\customcal{E}(\theta)$ is well defined is called the \textit{natural parameter space} $\overline{\Theta}$.

nodes.name: Truncated estimation with unknown survival set
nodes.statement:
Suppose that the ``true'' distribution $\customcal{D}^\star$ is described by an unknown target parameter $\theta^\star$ in $\overline{\Theta}$, \textit{i.e.}{}, $\customcal{D}^\star=\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$. 
    Given samples from $\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$ truncated to unknown survival set $S^\star \in \hypo{S}$ that is guaranteed to have mass at least $\alpha>0$ under $\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$, \textit{i.e.}{}, $\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)(S^\star)\geq \alpha$, the goal is to recover an estimate of $\theta^\star$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Truncated Estimation with Unknown Survival Set
nodes.statement_short: Estimate theta* of an exponential family from samples truncated to an unknown set S* of mass at least alpha.
also_stated_at:
One important goal in truncated statistics is to estimate the parameters of a distribution when samples are observed only if they fall in some \textit{unknown} survival set $S^\star\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$.
        A bit more formally, 
        there is a parametric family $\hypo{D}=\inbrace{\customcal{D}(\theta)\colon \theta}$ with target parameter $\theta^\star$. 
        The goal is to find an estimate $\wh{\theta}$ of $\theta^\star$ given samples from the truncation\footnote{The truncation of a distribution $\customcal{D}$ to a set $S$ is the conditional distribution of $\customcal{D}$, conditioned on the event that a point lies in $S$. When $\customcal{D}$ has a density, the truncated density is given by $\frac{1}{\customcal{D}(S)} \cdot \mathds{1}\inparen{x \in S} \cdot \customcal{D}(x)$} of the target distribution $\customcal{D}^\star = \customcal{D}(\theta^\star)$ to the set $S^\star$ -- without \textit{any} access to $S^\star$.

nodes.statement:
Suppose \cref{asmp:exponentialFamily} (\cref{unknowntrunc:int,unknowntrunc:proj,unknowntrunc:fisher,unknowntrunc:st}) holds
        and  one has an efficient sampling oracle for $\customcal{E}$.\footnote{By this we mean that given any $\theta \in \Theta$, one can draw an independent sample $x$ from a distribution $\customcal{Q}$ satisfying $\tv{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{E}(\theta)}\leq \delta$ in $\mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{md}{\delta})$ time.} Fix $\varepsilon, \delta \in (0, \nfrac{1}{2})$ and $k$ such that degree-$k$ polynomials $\varepsilon^{D}$-approximate $S^\star$ with respect to family $\customcal{E}$ in $L_1$-norm for $D=\mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{\Lambda}{\alpha \eta \lambda})$
        and $n = \mathrm{poly}(d^k, \varepsilon^{-D}, \log \nfrac{1}{\delta})$. There is an algorithm that given $\varepsilon, \delta$, constants $(\lambda,\Lambda,\deg(t(\cdot)),\eta,\alpha)$, and $n$ independent samples from $\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$ truncated to $S^\star$, in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time, outputs an estimate $\theta$ such that with probability $1-\delta$,
        \[
            \tv{\customcal{E}(\theta)}{\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)} \leq \varepsilon\,.
        \]

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.3
nodes.statement:
This result follows by combining \cref{thm:main} with the reduction in Corollary 6.13 in the arXiv version of \cite{lee2024unknown}.
        The reduction converts the estimation problem in \cref{cor:truncation} to the following learning problem in $\mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{d}{(\varepsilon\alpha)})$ time:
            given samples from a distribution $\customcal{D}=\customcal{E}(\theta_0)$ that is close to $\customcal{D}^\star=\customcal{E}(\theta^\star)$ in a sense stronger than that of \cref{asmp:smoothness} with $\nfrac{1}{\sigma}=q=C$ for $C=\mathrm{poly}\inparen{\nfrac{\Lambda}{(\alpha\eta\lambda)}}$, find a set $S$ such that $\customcal{D}^\star(S\triangle S^\star)\leq \varepsilon^{O(C)}$.
        This precisely fits into the framework of PIU learning with ${H^\star}=S^\star$ and, moreover, since in the model of \citet{lee2024unknown}, $\customcal{D}^\star(S^\star)\geq \alpha$ which ensures \cref{asmp:posFraction} holds allowing us to apply \cref{thm:main} directly.

nodes.name: Detecting Truncation with Exact Samples
nodes.statement:
Fix constant $\beta\in (0,1)$, set $S^\star\in \hypo{S} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, and distribution $\customcal{Q}$ over $\mathbb{R}^d$, such that, $\customcal{Q}(S^\star)\leq 1-\beta$.
            The following holds. 
                    Let $k$ be such that degree-$k$ polynomials $\zeta$-approximate $\hypo{S}$ in $L_1$-norm with respect to $\customcal{Q}$ for $\zeta\leq \beta^4 \varepsilon^{5}$.
                    There is an algorithm that given $\beta,\delta,k$ and $n=\mathrm{poly}(d^k,\nfrac{1}{\zeta},\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})$ samples (a) $\customcal{D}\in\inbrace{\customcal{Q},\customcal{Q}(S^\star)}$ and (b) $\customcal{Q}$, with probability $1-\delta$, correctly detects whether $\customcal{D}=\customcal{Q}$ or $\customcal{Q}=\customcal{Q}(S^\star)$.
                    The algorithm runs in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time.

nodes.name: Detecting Truncation with Approximate Samples
nodes.statement:
Consider the setting in \cref{cor:detectingTruncation}.
            Let $\customcal{R}$ be a distribution such that $\customcal{Q}$ is $(\sigma,q)$-smooth with respect to $\customcal{R}$ (\textit{i.e.}{}, for any measurable set $S$, $\customcal{Q}(S)\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\cdot \customcal{R}(S)^{1/q}$).
                    Let $k$ be such that degree-$k$ polynomials $\zeta$-approximate $\hypo{S}$ in $L_1$-norm with respect to $\customcal{Q}$ for $\zeta\leq ({\sigma\alpha^2}{})^{2q}\cdot \varepsilon^{1+4q}$.
                    There is an algorithm that given $\beta,\delta,k$ and $n$ samples (a) $\customcal{D}\in\inbrace{\customcal{Q},\customcal{Q}(S^\star)}$ and (b) $\customcal{R}$, with probability $1-\delta$, correctly detects whether $\customcal{D}=\customcal{Q}$ or $\customcal{Q}=\customcal{Q}(S^\star)$.
                    The algorithm runs in $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ time.

nodes.statement: Recall that a halfspace is a Boolean function $h\colon \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \{0, 1\}$ of the form $h(x) = \mathds{1}\sinbrace{w^\top x + t \geq 0}$ for some vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and threshold $t\in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Intersection of halfspaces
nodes.statement: An intersection of $k$ halfspaces $h_1,h_2,\dots,h_k$ is the Boolean function formed by taking the logical AND of the halfspaces, \textit{i.e.}{}, $h_1(x)\cdot h_2(x)\cdot \dots\cdot h_k(x)$.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Functions of Halfspaces
nodes.statement: The concept class of functions of halfspaces consists of all Boolean functions of the form $b(h_1,h_2,\dots,h_k)$ where $b\colon \ensuremath{\inbrace{0, 1}}^k\to \ensuremath{\inbrace{0, 1}}$ is an arbitrary boolean function and $h_1,h_2,\dots,h_k$ are any $k$ halfspaces.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Decision Tree
nodes.statement:
A decision tree is a rooted binary tree in which each internal node is labeled with a variable $x_i$ (for $1\leq i\leq d$) and has two children. 
        Each leaf is labeled with an output from $\{0, 1\}$.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Boolean function computed by a decision tree
nodes.statement: A decision tree computes a Boolean function in the following standard way: Given an input $x \in \{0,1\}^d$, the value of the function on $x$ is the output in the leaf reached by the path that starts at the root and goes left or right at each internal node according to whether the variable’s value in $x$ is 0 or 1, respectively.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm
nodes.definiendum: function computed by a decision tree

nodes.name: Size of a decision tree
nodes.statement: The \textit{size} of a decision tree is the number of leaves of the tree.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Depth of a node
nodes.statement: The \textit{depth} of a node in a decision tree is the number of edges in the path from the root to the node.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Depth of a decision tree
nodes.statement: The \textit{depth of the tree} is the maximum depth of one of its leaves.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm

nodes.name: Depth bounds size of decision trees
nodes.statement: Observe that a decision tree of depth $d$ has size at most $2^d$.
nodes.section: B Additional Preliminaries and the \textsf{L1-Regression}{} Algorithm
assumptions: a decision tree of depth $d$
conclusions: has size at most $2^d$

A decision tree of halfspaces is a rooted binary tree in which each internal node $i$ is labeled with a halfspace $h_{i_j}$ (for $1\leq i\leq d$) and has two children. 
        Each leaf is labeled with an output from $\{0, 1\}$.

nodes.name: Agnostic Pessimistic-ERM guarantee
nodes.statement:
Suppose \cref{asmp:posFraction,asmp:smoothness} hold, allow ${H^\star}\not\in \hypo{H}$, and define $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\coloneqq \inf_{H\in \hypo{H}} \customcal{D}^\star(H\triangle {H^\star})$.
        Fix any parameters $\varepsilon,\delta, \gamma \in (0,\nfrac{1}{2})$ with $\varepsilon\geq \gamma > {\nfrac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}{\alpha}}$.  
        Consider the Pessimistic-ERM{} instance defined with respect to $n=\wt{O}\inparen{\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon}}\cdot \inparen{\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H})+\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}}$  positive and unlabeled samples obtained from the two streams in the PIU learning model (\cref{prob:PUlearning}).
        Then, with probability $1-\delta$, any hypothesis $H\in \hypo{H}$ that satisfies:
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= \gamma $; and 
            \item $H$ is optimal (though not necessarily feasible) for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho= {5\varepsilon} $,
        \end{enumerate}
        also satisfies
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{H\triangle {H^\star}} \leq 
                \frac{144}{\sigma^2}\cdot \, \varepsilon^{1/q^2}
                \,.
        \]

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem C.1
nodes.statement:
The proof of \cref{new:thm:perm:robust} is divided into two parts: \cref{lem:perm:easy} bounds $\customcal{D}^\star(H \backslash H^\star)$ and \cref{lem:perm:hard} bounds $\customcal{D}^\star(H^\star \backslash H)$.
        Taking a union bound over the events in \cref{lem:perm:easy,lem:perm:hard} and recalling that ${H^\star}\triangle H=\inparen{H\setminus {H^\star}}\cup \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H}$ completes the proof of \cref{new:thm:perm:robust}.

nodes.name: Upper Bound on False Negative Error
nodes.statement:
Fix any $\eta\in (0,1).$
            Under the setting of \cref{new:thm:perm:robust}, consider any hypothesis $T\in \hypo{H}$ feasible for the Pessimistic-ERM{} instance in \cref{new:thm:perm:robust} with tolerance $\rho=\eta$.
            Then, with probability $1-\inparen{\nfrac{\delta}{2}}$,
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star}\setminus T} \leq \eta+\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]
            In particular, for $T=H$ and $\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, with probability $1-\inparen{\nfrac{\delta}{2}}$, $\customcal{D}^\star\inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H}\leq 3\varepsilon$.

nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.2
nodes.statement:
Let $T\in\hypo{H}$ be any solution of Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\eta$. By feasibility, it satisfies $\nfrac{\abs{ T \cap P}}{\abs{P}}\geq 1- \eta $ and, hence, $\nfrac{\abs{ P\setminus T}}{\abs{P}}\leq \eta$.
            Due to the choice of the sample size $n$ and \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, with probability $1-\inparen{\nfrac{\delta}{2}}$, for each $R\in \hypo{H}\cup \inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$,\footnote{Here, we use the facts that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}=\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_1\cup\hypo{H}_2)}\leq {\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_1)}+\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H}_2)}+1}$ \cite{mohri2018foundations}.}
            \[
                \customcal{P}^\star(R) 
                \leq 
                \frac{\abs{R\cap P}}{\abs{P}}
                +
                \sqrt{\frac{\abs{R\cap P}}{\abs{P}}\cdot \varepsilon}
                + \varepsilon\,.
            \]
            In particular, applying this to $R=T^c$ (note that $T^c\in\{G^c: G\in \hypo{H}\}$), and using $\nfrac{\abs{ P\cap T^c}}{\abs{P}}=\nfrac{\abs{ P\setminus T}}{\abs{P}}\leq \eta$, implies that 
            \[
                \customcal{P}^\star(T^c) \leq \eta+\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]
            Finally, since $\customcal{D}^\star( R )\leq \customcal{P}^\star( R )$ for any $ R \subseteq {H^\star}$, it follows that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus  T )
                \leq \customcal{P}^\star({H^\star}\setminus  T )
                = \customcal{P}^\star(T^c)
                \leq  \eta +\sqrt{\eta\varepsilon}+\varepsilon\,.
            \]

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.3
nodes.statement:
Our goal is to upper bound the mass of $H\setminus {H^\star}$ under $\customcal{D}^\star$. 
            One natural idea is to use the fact the $\varepsilon$-optimality of $H$ for Pessimistic-ERM{}, \textit{i.e.}{},  $\customcal{D}(H)$ is smaller than $\customcal{D}(H')$ for any other $H'$ feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{}, and then convert from $\customcal{D}$ to $
            \customcal{D}^\star$ via \cref{asmp:smoothness}.
            This approach does not go through as ${H^\star}$ is not guaranteed to be feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} (recall that in \cref{new:thm:perm:robust} we do not assume that ${H^\star}\in \hypo{H}$). 
            
            Instead, we construct a hypothesis $H'$ that is both ``close'' to ${H^\star}$ and is also feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{}.
            Recalling that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\coloneqq \inf_{H'\in \hypo{H}}\customcal{D}^\star(H'\triangle {H^\star})$, one can see that for any $\zeta>0$, there is an hypothesis $H'=H'_\zeta$ in $\hypo{H}$ satisfying
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} 
                \leq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} + \zeta\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            Consider any $0<\zeta\leq \alpha\varepsilon$ satisfying $\gamma \geq \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+\zeta}{\alpha}$, which exists since $\gamma > \nfrac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}{\alpha}$.
            Fix $H'=H'_\zeta$ for the remainder of the proof.
            We now show that, with high probability, $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho=O(\varepsilon)$.
            \begin{lemma}[Feasibility of $H'$] Let $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ be the event that the uniform convergence bounds in \cref{thm:unifConvergence} hold for the positive samples $P$ and the hypothesis class $\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$.
                Then, $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}]\geq 1-(\nfrac{\delta}{4})$.
                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} defined by samples $(P,U)$ with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
            \end{lemma}
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:feasibility}]
                The lower bound on the probability of event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ follows directly from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}.
                We now prove the feasibility of $H'$.
                Since $\customcal{P}^\star$ is a truncation of $\customcal{D}^\star$ to ${H^\star}$, $ \customcal{P}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \nfrac{\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}}{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}\leq \nfrac{\inparen{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+ \zeta }}{{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}}$ and, further, since $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq  \alpha $, 
                \[
                    \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}\,.
                \]
                Condition on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$.
                The uniform convergence bound from \cref{thm:unifConvergence} implies that 
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c}
                        + \sqrt{ \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Combining the last two inequalities implies
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}
                        + \sqrt{ \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Further as $\zeta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\leq \alpha\varepsilon$ and $0<\alpha\leq 1$, we have $\nfrac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq 5\varepsilon$ which ensures the feasibility of $H'$.
            \end{proof}
            Now, we are ready to upper bound the mass of $H\setminus {H^\star}$ under $\customcal{D}$.
            For this, we decompose $H\setminus {H^\star}$
            \[
                H\setminus {H^\star} 
                    = H - {H^\star} + \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H}
                    = \inparen{H - H'} 
                        + \inparen{H' - {H^\star}} 
                        + \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H}\,,
            \]
            so that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}\inparen{H\setminus {H^\star}}
                    = \inparen{
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{H} -    \customcal{D}\inparen{H'}
                      } + 
                      \inparen{
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{H'} - \customcal{D}\inparen{{H^\star}}
                      } +
                      \customcal{D}\inparen{{{H^\star} \setminus H}}\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            The bulk of the remaining proof will focus on bounding the first term; before that, we turn to upper bounding the second and third terms. 
            \begin{lemma} Conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ from \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:feasibility}, the following bounds hold
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H') - \customcal{D}({H^\star}) \leq \frac{1}{\sigma}\cdot \inparen{2\varepsilon}^{\sfrac{1}{q}} 
                    \qquadtext{and}
                    \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)
                    \leq \frac{1}{\sigma}\cdot\inparen{3\varepsilon}^{1/q}\,.
                \]
            \end{lemma}
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23}]
                As $\customcal{D}\sinparen{H'} - \customcal{D}\inparen{{H^\star}}\leq \customcal{D}\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}$, \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies that 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}\sinparen{H'} - \customcal{D}\inparen{{H^\star}}
                    \leq \customcal{D}\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}
                    \leq \frac{1}{\sigma}\cdot \customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}^{\sfrac{1}{q}}
                    \,.
                \]
                By the definition of $H'$ (\cref{eq:perm:closeToInf}), 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}\inparen{H'} - \customcal{D}\inparen{{H^\star}}
                    \leq \frac{1}{\sigma} \inparen{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+{ \zeta }}^{\sfrac{1}{q}}
                    \quad\Stackrel{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}},~\zeta\leq \varepsilon}{\leq}\quad \frac{1}{\sigma}\inparen{2\varepsilon}^{1/q}\,.
                \]
                Next, since $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with tolerance $\rho=\gamma$, \cref{lem:perm:easy} implies that, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq \gamma +\sqrt{\gamma\varepsilon}+\varepsilon$.
                Since $\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, we deduce $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq 3\varepsilon$.
                Applying \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies the result.
            \end{proof} 
            Next, we upper bound the first term in \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:decomposition}.
            \begin{lemma} Let $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ be the event that the uniform convergence bounds in \cref{thm:unifConvergence} hold for both the positive samples $P$ and the unlabeled samples $U$, and the hypothesis classes $\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$.
                Then, $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]\geq 1-(\nfrac{\delta}{4})$.
                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, 
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H) - \customcal{D}(H')
                    \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                    \,.
                \]
            \end{lemma}
            Note that \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23,lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterm1} imply that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}\inparen{H\setminus {H^\star}}
                    \leq 
                    \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(2\varepsilon)^{1/q}
                    + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(3\varepsilon)^{1/q}
                    + \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                    \leq \frac{13}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
            \]
            Now, \cref{lem:perm:hard} follows by using \cref{asmp:smoothness}.

            It remains to prove \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterm1}.
            The key idea is that $H$ is $\varepsilon$-optimal for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$ while $H'$ is feasible (\cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:feasibility}), and, hence,
            \[
                \frac{\abs{H\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                \leq 
                \frac{\abs{H'\cap U}}{\abs{U}}\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            Now, one can control $\customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')$ by combining uniform convergence and the above result.
            However, this requires $O(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon^2})$ samples since the error of $H'$, $\customcal{D}(H')$, may not be small. 
            To get the optimal sample complexity of $O(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})$, we use the fact that both $H$ and $H'$ are close to ${H^\star}$, \textit{i.e.}{}, their errors are small for the labeling $\mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in {H^\star}},$ and then use the second-order uniform convergence bounds (\cref{thm:unifConvergence}).
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterm1}]
                The lower bound on $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]$ follows from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, the choice of the sample size $n$, and the fact that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$\footnote{To see this, fix any sets $A,B,C.$
                    Let \(\hypo{F}=\{G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). For any finite set of samples \(X\), define the labelings \(L_{\hypo{H}}=\{X\cap G: G\in \hypo{H}\}\) and \(L_{\hypo{F}}=\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). 
                    Note that $\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}=\{(X\cap G)\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in{\hypo{H}}\}=\{L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):L\in L_{\hypo{H}}\}$
                    The map \(g\colon L_{\hypo{H}}\to L_{\hypo{F}}\) given by \(g(L)=L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)\) is injective, so \(|L_{\hypo{F}}|\le |L_{\hypo{H}}|\).} and, hence,
                \[
                    \textrm{\rm VC}{\bbinparen{\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}}}
                    \leq O(\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})})
                    \,.
                \] 
                Define 
                \[
                    T = {H^\star} \cap H\cap H'\,.
                \]
                Since
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H) = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                    \qquadtext{and}
                    \customcal{D}(H') = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(
                    H'\setminus T)\,,
                \]
                we have
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')
                    = 
                    \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)-\customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                We now bound $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$ in two steps.

                \paragraph{Step 1 (Upper bound on $\nfrac{\abs{U\setminus T}}{\abs{U}}$).}
                    Notice that 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        = \customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \end{align*}
                    \cref{eq:perm:closeToInf} and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}},~\zeta\leq \varepsilon$ imply that $\customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon$.
                    Therefore, 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \]
                    Further, since ${H^\star}\setminus T \subseteq \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H'} \cup \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H}$,
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star} \setminus T)\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')+ \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                    \]
                    Therefore, 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon 
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*}
                    We have the following upper bounds on the last two terms:
                    \begin{enumerate}
                        \item Since $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23}, implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,\sinparen{3\varepsilon}^{1/q}$.
                        (Here, we use the fact that $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ by construction.)
                        \item Conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ (which implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$), $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
                        Hence, \cref{lem:perm:easy} implies that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq 5\varepsilon + \sqrt{5}\cdot \varepsilon+\varepsilon\leq 9\varepsilon $.
                        Finally, \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}$.
                    \end{enumerate}
                    Condition only event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$.
                    Substituting the above two bounds into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm3:step1}, implies that 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T) \leq 2\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(3\varepsilon)^{1/q} + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{}{\leq}~~~ 2\varepsilon + \frac{2}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{q\geq 1}{\leq}~~~
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over the unlabeled samples and hypotheses class $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\cdot \varepsilon}
                        +
                        \varepsilon 
                        =
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Since $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$ (as $q\geq 1$), $9\varepsilon \leq 1$ (which can be ensured by rescaling $\varepsilon$ by a constant factor), and $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}$, it follows that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3+\sqrt{3}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        \leq  \frac{6}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                \paragraph{Step 2 (Upper bound on $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$).}
                    \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:optimalityOfH} and the fact that for any set $S$, $\nfrac{\abs{(S\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}=\nfrac{\abs{S\cap (U\setminus T)}}{\abs{U}}$ implies that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Hence, \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:boundSamples} implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq  \frac{7}{\sigma}(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over $U$ and the hypothesis $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                        \leq 
                            \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            + \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q} \cdot \varepsilon}
                            + \varepsilon
                            = 
                                \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                                +
                                \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                                +\varepsilon \,.
                    \end{align*}
                    Noting again that $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}\leq 1$ and that the square root term can be absorbed as $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$, we obtain
                    \[
                            \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                            \leq \frac{7+\sqrt{7}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \,.
                    \]
                    Substituting this into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub} completes the proof.
            \end{proof}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.5
nodes.statement:
The lower bound on the probability of event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ follows directly from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}.
                We now prove the feasibility of $H'$.
                Since $\customcal{P}^\star$ is a truncation of $\customcal{D}^\star$ to ${H^\star}$, $ \customcal{P}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \nfrac{\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}}{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}\leq \nfrac{\inparen{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+ \zeta }}{{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}}$ and, further, since $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq  \alpha $, 
                \[
                    \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}\,.
                \]
                Condition on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$.
                The uniform convergence bound from \cref{thm:unifConvergence} implies that 
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c}
                        + \sqrt{ \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Combining the last two inequalities implies
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}
                        + \sqrt{ \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Further as $\zeta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\leq \alpha\varepsilon$ and $0<\alpha\leq 1$, we have $\nfrac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq 5\varepsilon$ which ensures the feasibility of $H'$.
