nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.7
nodes.statement:
The lower bound on $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]$ follows from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, the choice of the sample size $n$, and the fact that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$\footnote{To see this, fix any sets $A,B,C.$
                    Let \(\hypo{F}=\{G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). For any finite set of samples \(X\), define the labelings \(L_{\hypo{H}}=\{X\cap G: G\in \hypo{H}\}\) and \(L_{\hypo{F}}=\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). 
                    Note that $\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}=\{(X\cap G)\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in{\hypo{H}}\}=\{L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):L\in L_{\hypo{H}}\}$
                    The map \(g\colon L_{\hypo{H}}\to L_{\hypo{F}}\) given by \(g(L)=L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)\) is injective, so \(|L_{\hypo{F}}|\le |L_{\hypo{H}}|\).} and, hence,
                \[
                    \textrm{\rm VC}{\bbinparen{\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}}}
                    \leq O(\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})})
                    \,.
                \] 
                Define 
                \[
                    T = {H^\star} \cap H\cap H'\,.
                \]
                Since
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H) = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                    \qquadtext{and}
                    \customcal{D}(H') = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(
                    H'\setminus T)\,,
                \]
                we have
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')
                    = 
                    \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)-\customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                We now bound $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$ in two steps.

                \paragraph{Step 1 (Upper bound on $\nfrac{\abs{U\setminus T}}{\abs{U}}$).}
                    Notice that 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        = \customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \end{align*}
                    \cref{eq:perm:closeToInf} and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}},~\zeta\leq \varepsilon$ imply that $\customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon$.
                    Therefore, 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \]
                    Further, since ${H^\star}\setminus T \subseteq \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H'} \cup \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H}$,
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star} \setminus T)\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')+ \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                    \]
                    Therefore, 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon 
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*}
                    We have the following upper bounds on the last two terms:
                    \begin{enumerate}
                        \item Since $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23}, implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,\sinparen{3\varepsilon}^{1/q}$.
                        (Here, we use the fact that $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ by construction.)
                        \item Conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ (which implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$), $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
                        Hence, \cref{lem:perm:easy} implies that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq 5\varepsilon + \sqrt{5}\cdot \varepsilon+\varepsilon\leq 9\varepsilon $.
                        Finally, \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}$.
                    \end{enumerate}
                    Condition only event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$.
                    Substituting the above two bounds into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm3:step1}, implies that 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T) \leq 2\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(3\varepsilon)^{1/q} + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{}{\leq}~~~ 2\varepsilon + \frac{2}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{q\geq 1}{\leq}~~~
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over the unlabeled samples and hypotheses class $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\cdot \varepsilon}
                        +
                        \varepsilon 
                        =
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Since $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$ (as $q\geq 1$), $9\varepsilon \leq 1$ (which can be ensured by rescaling $\varepsilon$ by a constant factor), and $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}$, it follows that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3+\sqrt{3}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        \leq  \frac{6}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                \paragraph{Step 2 (Upper bound on $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$).}
                    \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:optimalityOfH} and the fact that for any set $S$, $\nfrac{\abs{(S\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}=\nfrac{\abs{S\cap (U\setminus T)}}{\abs{U}}$ implies that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Hence, \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:boundSamples} implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq  \frac{7}{\sigma}(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over $U$ and the hypothesis $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                        \leq 
                            \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            + \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q} \cdot \varepsilon}
                            + \varepsilon
                            = 
                                \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                                +
                                \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                                +\varepsilon \,.
                    \end{align*}
                    Noting again that $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}\leq 1$ and that the square root term can be absorbed as $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$, we obtain
                    \[
                            \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                            \leq \frac{7+\sqrt{7}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \,.
                    \]
                    Substituting this into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub} completes the proof.

nodes.name: Why the direct approach fails
nodes.statement:
Our goal is to upper bound the mass of $H\setminus {H^\star}$ under $\customcal{D}^\star$. 
            One natural idea is to use the fact the $\varepsilon$-optimality of $H$ for Pessimistic-ERM{}, \textit{i.e.}{},  $\customcal{D}(H)$ is smaller than $\customcal{D}(H')$ for any other $H'$ feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{}, and then convert from $\customcal{D}$ to $
            \customcal{D}^\star$ via \cref{asmp:smoothness}.
            This approach does not go through as ${H^\star}$ is not guaranteed to be feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} (recall that in \cref{new:thm:perm:robust} we do not assume that ${H^\star}\in \hypo{H}$).

nodes.name: Construct H' close to H*
nodes.statement:
Instead, we construct a hypothesis $H'$ that is both ``close'' to ${H^\star}$ and is also feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{}.
            Recalling that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\coloneqq \inf_{H'\in \hypo{H}}\customcal{D}^\star(H'\triangle {H^\star})$, one can see that for any $\zeta>0$, there is an hypothesis $H'=H'_\zeta$ in $\hypo{H}$ satisfying
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} 
                \leq \ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} + \zeta\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            Consider any $0<\zeta\leq \alpha\varepsilon$ satisfying $\gamma \geq \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+\zeta}{\alpha}$, which exists since $\gamma > \nfrac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}{\alpha}$.
            Fix $H'=H'_\zeta$ for the remainder of the proof.

nodes.name: Lemma C.5 and its proof

                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$, $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} defined by samples $(P,U)$ with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
            \end{lemma}
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:feasibility}]
                The lower bound on the probability of event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ follows directly from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}.
                We now prove the feasibility of $H'$.
                Since $\customcal{P}^\star$ is a truncation of $\customcal{D}^\star$ to ${H^\star}$, $ \customcal{P}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \nfrac{\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}}}{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}\leq \nfrac{\inparen{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}+ \zeta }}{{\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})}}$ and, further, since $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq  \alpha $, 
                \[
                    \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{H'\triangle {H^\star}} \leq \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}\,.
                \]
                Condition on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$.
                The uniform convergence bound from \cref{thm:unifConvergence} implies that 
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c}
                        + \sqrt{ \customcal{P}^\star\inparen{{H'}^c} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Combining the last two inequalities implies
                \[
                    \frac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq
                        \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha}
                        + \sqrt{ \frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}} +  \zeta }{\alpha} \cdot \varepsilon}
                        + \varepsilon\,.
                \]
                Further as $\zeta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}\leq \alpha\varepsilon$ and $0<\alpha\leq 1$, we have $\nfrac{\abs{P\setminus H'}}{\abs{P}}
                    \leq 5\varepsilon$ which ensures the feasibility of $H'$.
            \end{proof}

nodes.name: Lemma C.7
nodes.statement:
Next, we upper bound the first term in \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:decomposition}.
            \begin{lemma} Let $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ be the event that the uniform convergence bounds in \cref{thm:unifConvergence} hold for both the positive samples $P$ and the unlabeled samples $U$, and the hypothesis classes $\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$.
                Then, $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]\geq 1-(\nfrac{\delta}{4})$.
                Moreover, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$,

                    \customcal{D}(H) - \customcal{D}(H')
                    \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                    \,.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.7
nodes.statement:
It remains to prove \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterm1}.
            The key idea is that $H$ is $\varepsilon$-optimal for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$ while $H'$ is feasible (\cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:feasibility}), and, hence,
            \[
                \frac{\abs{H\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                \leq 
                \frac{\abs{H'\cap U}}{\abs{U}}\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
            Now, one can control $\customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')$ by combining uniform convergence and the above result.
            However, this requires $O(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon^2})$ samples since the error of $H'$, $\customcal{D}(H')$, may not be small. 
            To get the optimal sample complexity of $O(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})$, we use the fact that both $H$ and $H'$ are close to ${H^\star}$, \textit{i.e.}{}, their errors are small for the labeling $\mathds{1}\sinbrace{x\in {H^\star}},$ and then use the second-order uniform convergence bounds (\cref{thm:unifConvergence}).
            \begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterm1}]
                The lower bound on $\Pr[\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}]$ follows from \cref{thm:unifConvergence}, the choice of the sample size $n$, and the fact that $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$ and $\textrm{\rm VC}{(\inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}})}\leq \textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})}$\footnote{To see this, fix any sets $A,B,C.$
                    Let \(\hypo{F}=\{G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). For any finite set of samples \(X\), define the labelings \(L_{\hypo{H}}=\{X\cap G: G\in \hypo{H}\}\) and \(L_{\hypo{F}}=\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}\). 
                    Note that $\{X\cap (G\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in \hypo{H}\}=\{(X\cap G)\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)):G\in{\hypo{H}}\}=\{L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C):L\in L_{\hypo{H}}\}$
                    The map \(g\colon L_{\hypo{H}}\to L_{\hypo{F}}\) given by \(g(L)=L\setminus (A\cap B\cap C)\) is injective, so \(|L_{\hypo{F}}|\le |L_{\hypo{H}}|\).} and, hence,
                \[
                    \textrm{\rm VC}{\bbinparen{\hypo{H}\cup\inbrace{G^c\colon G\in \hypo{H}}\cup \inbrace{G\setminus ({H^\star} \cap H\cap H')\colon G\in \hypo{H}}}}
                    \leq O(\textrm{\rm VC}{(\hypo{H})})
                    \,.
                \] 
                Define 
                \[
                    T = {H^\star} \cap H\cap H'\,.
                \]
                Since
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H) = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                    \qquadtext{and}
                    \customcal{D}(H') = \customcal{D}(T) + \customcal{D}(
                    H'\setminus T)\,,
                \]
                we have
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(H)-\customcal{D}(H')
                    = 
                    \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)-\customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)\,.
                    \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                We now bound $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$ in two steps.

                \paragraph{Step 1 (Upper bound on $\nfrac{\abs{U\setminus T}}{\abs{U}}$).}
                    Notice that 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        = \customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \end{align*}
                    \cref{eq:perm:closeToInf} and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}},~\zeta\leq \varepsilon$ imply that $\customcal{D}(H'\setminus {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon$.
                    Therefore, 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon
                        + \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\,.
                    \]
                    Further, since ${H^\star}\setminus T \subseteq \inparen{{H^\star} \setminus H'} \cup \inparen{{H^\star}\setminus H}$,
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}\inparen{\sinparen{H'\cap {H^\star}}\setminus T}\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star} \setminus T)\leq \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')+ \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                    \]
                    Therefore, 
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T)
                        \leq 2\varepsilon 
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')
                        + \customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \end{align*}
                    We have the following upper bounds on the last two terms:
                    \begin{enumerate}
                        \item Since $H$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=\gamma\leq \varepsilon$, conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$, \cref{lem:sampleComplexity:Hard:UBterms23}, implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H)\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,\sinparen{3\varepsilon}^{1/q}$.
                        (Here, we use the fact that $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$ by construction.)
                        \item Conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$ (which implies $\ensuremath{\mathscr{E}}$), $H'$ is feasible for Pessimistic-ERM{} with $\rho=5\varepsilon$.
                        Hence, \cref{lem:perm:easy} implies that $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq 5\varepsilon + \sqrt{5}\cdot \varepsilon+\varepsilon\leq 9\varepsilon $.
                        Finally, \cref{asmp:smoothness} implies that $\customcal{D}({H^\star}\setminus H')\leq (\nfrac{1}{\sigma})\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}$.
                    \end{enumerate}
                    Condition only event $\ensuremath{\mathscr{F}}$.
                    Substituting the above two bounds into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm3:step1}, implies that 
                    \[
                        \customcal{D}(H'\setminus T) \leq 2\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(3\varepsilon)^{1/q} + \frac{1}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{}{\leq}~~~ 2\varepsilon + \frac{2}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        ~~~\Stackrel{q\geq 1}{\leq}~~~
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over the unlabeled samples and hypotheses class $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\cdot \varepsilon}
                        +
                        \varepsilon 
                        =
                        \frac{3}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        + 
                        \sqrt{\frac{3}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Since $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$ (as $q\geq 1$), $9\varepsilon \leq 1$ (which can be ensured by rescaling $\varepsilon$ by a constant factor), and $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}$, it follows that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{3+\sqrt{3}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                        \leq  \frac{6}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                        \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
                \paragraph{Step 2 (Upper bound on $\customcal{D}(H\setminus T)$).}
                    \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:optimalityOfH} and the fact that for any set $S$, $\nfrac{\abs{(S\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}=\nfrac{\abs{S\cap (U\setminus T)}}{\abs{U}}$ implies that 
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq 
                        \frac{\abs{(H'\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        +\varepsilon\,.
                    \]
                    Hence, \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:boundSamples} implies that,
                    \[
                        \frac{\abs{(H\setminus T)\cap U}}{\abs{U}}
                        \leq  \frac{7}{\sigma}(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}\,.
                    \]
                    Now, uniform convergence over $U$ and the hypothesis $\inbrace{G\setminus T\colon G\in \hypo{H}}$ implies that,
                    \begin{align*}
                        \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                        \leq 
                            \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            + \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q} \cdot \varepsilon}
                            + \varepsilon
                            = 
                                \frac{7}{\sigma}\,(9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                                +
                                \sqrt{\frac{7}{\sigma}}\,(9\varepsilon )^{\frac{1+q}{2q}}
                                +\varepsilon \,.
                    \end{align*}
                    Noting again that $\sigma\leq \sqrt{\sigma}\leq 1$ and that the square root term can be absorbed as $\nfrac{1}{q}\leq \nfrac{(1+q)}{2q}$, we obtain
                    \[
                            \customcal{D}(H\setminus T)
                            \leq \frac{7+\sqrt{7}+1}{\sigma}\, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \leq \frac{11}{\sigma} \, (9\varepsilon )^{1/q}
                            \,.
                    \]
                    Substituting this into \cref{eq:sampleComplexity:UBterm1:ub} completes the proof.
            \end{proof}

nodes.statement:
To see that most common hypothesis classes satisfy the above requirement and, hence, are not learnable from positive samples alone, note that intersections of $k$ one-dimensional intervals or intersections of $k$ two-dimensional halfspaces have a VC dimension $\Omega(k)$, which tends to $\infty$ with $k$.
    Moreover, this also implies that any hypothesis class containing one-dimensional intervals or two-dimensional halfspaces (\textit{e.g.}{}, decision trees) are also not learnable from positive examples.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement:
Consider any $k\geq 1$.
        We reduce the problem of realizable $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$} from (labeled) samples $(x,y)$ where $x\sim \customcal{D}^\star$ to $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}$} from \textit{only} positive examples under the assumptions in the theorem.
        
        This reduction will work when the optimal hypothesis ${H^\star}$ has sufficient mass in given PAC learning instance, in particular, $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$.
        The desired result can be deduced from this reduction due to the following sample complexity lower bound for learning intersections of $k$ halfspaces by taking the limit $k\to\infty$.
        \begin{theorem}[\protect{\cite[Theorem 5.3]{neuralNetwork2009bartlett}}] The sample complexity of $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-PAC learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$} under the assumption that $\customcal{D}({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ is $S_{\varepsilon,\delta}(k)\coloneqq \wt{\Omega}\inparen{(\nfrac{1}{\varepsilon})(\textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H}_{\cap k})+\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}})}$ for $\varepsilon<\nfrac{1}{8}$ and $\delta < \nfrac{1}{100}$.
                {In particular, if $\lim_{k\to \infty} \textrm{\rm VC}{}(\hypo{H}_{\cap k})=\infty$, then $\lim_{k\to \infty} S_{\varepsilon,\delta}(k)=\infty$.}
        \end{theorem}
        \begin{proof}[Proof sketch of \cref{thm:PAClearningLowerbound}]
                The proof follows by verifying that the hard instance created in Theorem 5.3 of \cite{neuralNetwork2009bartlett} satisfies $\customcal{D}({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ and that the VC-dimension of {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$ goes to $\infty$ with $k$ by definition}. 
            \end{proof}
        

        \noindent In the remainder of the proof, we describe the reduction and prove its correctness.

        \paragraph{Reduction.}
        Fix an instance of PAC-learning {$\hypo{H}_{\cap k}$}, covariate distribution $\customcal{D}^\star$, and the optimal set ${H^\star}$ satisfying $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$.
        The reduction is as follows.
        \begin{mdframed}
            \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=-1pt]
                \item[]  \hspace{-6mm} \textbf{Input:} 
                    An accuracy parameter $\varepsilon>0$, a confidence parameter $\delta>0$, and
                    $n$ labeled samples $\inbrace{\inparen{x_i,y_i}\colon 1\leq i\leq n}$ where $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ are i.i.d.{} from $\customcal{D}$ and $y_i=\mathds{1}\sinbrace{x_i\in {H^\star}}$
                \item[]  \hspace{-6mm}  \textbf{Oracle Access:}
                    Query access to a PAC learner $\customcal{L}$ that learns from only positive samples 
                \vspace{2mm}
                \item Let the set of positive examples be $P=\inbrace{x_i \colon i\in \inbrace{1, 2, \dots,n},~~~ y_i=1}$.
                \item Return the hypothesis $\wh{H}$ obtained by querying the learner $\customcal{L}$ with $\inparen{\varepsilon,\delta,P}$.
            \end{enumerate}
        \end{mdframed} 
        Since $\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$, we get that with high probability $\abs{P}\geq \Omega(n)$ and, hence, we only lose a constant factor of samples in the reduction.
        
        
        \paragraph{Soundness and Correctness.}
        To prove the correctness of the reduction, suppose $\wh{H}$ satisfies the requirement of PAC learning from positive examples:
            with probability $1-\delta$, 
            for each distribution $\customcal{D}'$, 
                satisfying $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$ and
                $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$, it holds that 
            \[
                \customcal{D}'(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq\varepsilon\,.
                \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
        We will show that it implies $\customcal{D}^\star\sinparen{\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star}}\leq 2\varepsilon$, proving the result.
        Let the optimal hypothesis be ${H^\star}=H^\star_1\cap H^\star_2\cap \dots \cap H^\star_k$ where $H^\star_1,H^\star_2,\dots,H^\star_k \in \hypo{H}$.
        Without loss of generality, suppose that there is no set $S\subsetneq[k]$ with ${H^\star}\neq \bigcap_{i\in S} H^\star_i$.
        Otherwise, we can select the smallest such $S$, and continue with the remainder of the proof with $k=\abs{S}$ and the halfspaces $\inbrace{H^\star_i \colon i\in S}$.
        Define the following sets, which are useful in the analysis:
        \[
            T_1 = \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus H^\star_1\,,\quad 
            T_2 = H^\star_1 \setminus H^\star_2\,,\quad 
            T_3 = \sinparen{H^\star_1\cap H^\star_2} \setminus H^\star_3\,,\quad \dots\quad 
            T_k = {\bigcap_{i=1}^{k-1}H^\star_i} \setminus H^\star_k
            \,.
        \]
        We will only need the following properties of $T_1,T_2,\dots,T_k$: for distinct $1\leq i,j\leq k$
        \[
            T_i \neq \emptyset\,,\quad 
            T_i \cap T_j = \emptyset\,,\quad 
            T_i \cap {H^\star} = \emptyset\,,\quadtext{and}
            T_i \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2\setminus H^\star_i\,.
            \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
        The first condition follows from the assumption that there is no set $S\subsetneq [k]$ with ${H^\star}=\bigcap_{i\in S}H^\star_i$.
        The remaining conditions follow from construction.
        Consider the following sequence of distributions: for each $1\leq i\leq k,$
        \[
            \customcal{D}'_i = \frac{1}{2}
                        \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}} + \frac{1}{2}\customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}\,,
        \]
        where, for each set $S$ and distribution $\customcal{Q}$, $\customcal{Q}_S$ is the truncation of $\customcal{Q}$ to $S$.
        First, we verify that $\customcal{D}'_i$ satisfies the guarantees specified above.
        \begin{fact}
            For each $1\leq i\leq k$, 
            $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})\geq \nfrac{1}{2}$, and 
            $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$. 
        \end{fact}
        \begin{proof}
            Fix any $1\leq i\leq k$.
            It holds that, $\customcal{D}'({H^\star})=\sfrac{\customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}({H^\star})}{2}=\nfrac{1}{2}$.
            Further, by construction, $\customcal{D}'_{{H^\star}}=\customcal{P}$.






            
            
            
            
        \end{proof}
        Now, using \cref{eq:lowerbound:PIUGuarantee} for each of $\customcal{D}'_1,\dots,\customcal{D}'_k$ implies that: for each $1\leq i\leq k$,
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            + 
            \customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            \leq 2\varepsilon\,.
        \]
        Hence, 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq 2\varepsilon
            \qquadtext{and}
            \max_{1\leq i\leq k}\customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            \leq 2\varepsilon\,.
            \addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \]
        Now, we are ready to bound $\customcal{D}^\star(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})\leq O(\varepsilon)$:
        \begin{align*}
            \customcal{D}^\star(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            &= \customcal{D}^\star({H^\star}) \customcal{D}^\star_{{H^\star}}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
            + \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star(T_i) \customcal{D}^\star_{T_i}(\wh{H}\triangle {H^\star})
                \tag{since $T_1,T_2,\dots,T_k,{H^\star}$ are disjoint; \textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:onesided:propertiesofT}}}}\\
            &\leq 2\customcal{D}^\star({H^\star})\varepsilon
            + 2\varepsilon \sum_i \customcal{D}^\star(T_i)
                \tag{by \textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:onesided:errorGuarantee}}}}\\
            &= 2\varepsilon\,.
        \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.11
nodes.statement:
Fix $\eta$ corresponding to the guarantee in \cref{lem:constReg:expectedValue}
                \[
                    \eta= O\inparen{\sqrt{\frac{1}{\alpha\sigma}}} \cdot \zeta^{1/(4q)}
                        + O\sinparen{\delta}\,.
                \]
                Observe that for each $i$, $\nfrac{\abs{H_i\cap U}}{\abs{U}}\geq 0$ and, hence, Markov's inequality implies that 
                \[
                    \Pr\insquare{\frac{\abs{H_i\cap U_i}}{\abs{U_i}} 
                    \geq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+2\eta} 
                    \leq {\frac{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+\eta}{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+2\eta}}\,.
                \]
                Hence, since each repetition of Subroutines A and B in \cref{alg:constReg} is independent, it follows that 
                \[
                    \Pr\insquare{
                        \min_{1\leq i\leq T}
                    \frac{\abs{H_i\cap U_i}}{\abs{U_i}} \geq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+2\eta 
                    } 
                    \leq \inparen{{\frac{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+\eta}{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+2\eta}}}^T
                    ~~~~~~\Stackrel{\substack{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})\leq 1,\\0\leq\eta\leq \nfrac{1}{2}}}{\leq}~~~~~~ 
                        \inparen{1-\frac{\eta}{2}}^T
                    \leq e^{-\frac{1}{2}\eta T}
                    \leq \delta
                    \,.
                \]
                Where in the last inequality, we used $T=O\inparen{\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\sqrt{\zeta}}}\log\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}$ and, hence, $\eta T\geq 2\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}$.
                Since with probability $1-\delta$, $\zeta$-uniform convergence holds with respect to each $U_1,U_2,\dots,U_T$ and hypothesis $\hypo{H}$ (see \cref{lem:constReg:unifConvergenceHoldsWHP}), it follows that with probability $1-2\delta$,
                \[
                    \Pr\insquare{
                    \min_{1\leq i\leq T} \customcal{D}(H_i) \geq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 2\eta + \zeta
                    }
                    \leq \delta\,.
                \]
                Define $\wh{H}=H_{i^\star}$ for $i^\star\in \operatornamewithlimits{arg\,min}_{1\leq i\leq T} \abs{H_i\cap U'}$.
                Now, uniform convergence, with respect to $\inbrace{H_1,\dots,H_N}$ and $U'$ implies that with probability $1-\delta$, $\abs{\customcal{D}(H_i) - \inparen{\nfrac{\abs{H_i\cap U_i'}}{\abs{U_i'}}}}\leq \zeta$ and, hence, with probability $1-3\delta$,
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(\wh{H})
                    \leq \frac{\sabs{\wh{H}\cap U'}}{\abs{U'}} + \zeta
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 2\eta + 3\zeta 
                    ~~\Stackrel{\zeta\leq \eta}{\leq}~~ \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 5\eta\,. 
                \]

                    } 
                    \leq \inparen{{\frac{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+\eta}{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})+2\eta}}}^T
                    ~~~~~~\Stackrel{\substack{\customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}})\leq 1,\\0\leq\eta\leq \nfrac{1}{2}}}{\leq}~~~~~~ 
                        \inparen{1-\frac{\eta}{2}}^T
                    \leq e^{-\frac{1}{2}\eta T}
                    \leq \delta
                    \,.
                \]
                Where in the last inequality, we used $T=O\inparen{\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\sqrt{\zeta}}}\log\inparen{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}}$ and, hence, $\eta T\geq 2\log{\nfrac{1}{\delta}}$.
nodes.section: E.2 Proof of 4.11 (Boosting via Repetition)

nodes.name: Uniform convergence (Lemma 4.7)
nodes.statement:
Since with probability $1-\delta$, $\zeta$-uniform convergence holds with respect to each $U_1,U_2,\dots,U_T$ and hypothesis $\hypo{H}$ (see \cref{lem:constReg:unifConvergenceHoldsWHP}), it follows that with probability $1-2\delta$,
                \[
                    \Pr\insquare{
                    \min_{1\leq i\leq T} \customcal{D}(H_i) \geq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 2\eta + \zeta
                    }
                    \leq \delta\,.
                \]
nodes.section: E.2 Proof of 4.11 (Boosting via Repetition)

nodes.name: Select on fresh samples
nodes.statement:
Define $\wh{H}=H_{i^\star}$ for $i^\star\in \operatornamewithlimits{arg\,min}_{1\leq i\leq T} \abs{H_i\cap U'}$.
                Now, uniform convergence, with respect to $\inbrace{H_1,\dots,H_N}$ and $U'$ implies that with probability $1-\delta$, $\abs{\customcal{D}(H_i) - \inparen{\nfrac{\abs{H_i\cap U_i'}}{\abs{U_i'}}}}\leq \zeta$ and, hence, with probability $1-3\delta$,
                \[
                    \customcal{D}(\wh{H})
                    \leq \frac{\sabs{\wh{H}\cap U'}}{\abs{U'}} + \zeta
                    \leq \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 2\eta + 3\zeta 
                    ~~\Stackrel{\zeta\leq \eta}{\leq}~~ \customcal{D}(H_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{OPT}}}) + 5\eta\,. 
                \]
nodes.section: E.2 Proof of 4.11 (Boosting via Repetition)

nodes.name: Constrained Regression as a linear program
nodes.statement:
Let $\hypo{R}$ be the set of all multisets $R\subseteq [d]$ of size at most $k$.
            For each $z\in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $R\in \hypo{R}$, define the monomial $z(R)\coloneqq \Pi_{i\in R} z_i$.
            For each monomial $z(R)$, let $c(R)$ be the corresponding coefficient in a polynomial $p$.
            The above program is equivalent to the following linear program.
            \begin{align*} 
                \min_{c\in \mathbb{R}^{\hypo{R}},\ z\in \mathbb{R}^{\abs{U}},\ w\in \mathbb{R}^{\abs{P}}}~
                    & {\sum_{x\in U} z(x)} \,,\\
                \forall_{x\in U}\,,\quad& \sum_{R\in \hypo{R}} c(R) x(R) ~\leq~ z(x) ~~\leq~ -\sum_{R\in \hypo{R}} c(R) x(R)\,,\\
                \forall_{x\in P}\,,\quad& \sum_{R\in \hypo{R}} c(R) x(R)~\leq~ w(x) ~\leq~ ~ 1\,,\\
                & {\frac{\sum_{x\in P} w(x)}{\abs{P}} \geq {1-\rho}}\,.
            \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma E.1
nodes.statement:
Fix measurable set $S$.
            Change of measure and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality imply that
            \[
                \customcal{D}^\star(S) 
                = \int \mathds{1}_S(x) \frac{\customcal{D}^\star(x)}{\customcal{D}(x)}{\rm d}\customcal{D}(x)
                \leq 
                    \inparen{
                        \int \mathds{1}_S(x)^{2}~ {\rm d}\customcal{D}(x)
                    }^{1/2}
                    \inparen{
                        \int \inparen{\frac{\customcal{D}^\star(x)}{\customcal{D}(x)}}^2 {\rm d} \customcal{D}(x)
                    }^{1/2}\,.
            \]
        Since $\mathds{1}_S(x)^{2}=\mathds{1}_S(x)$ and $
                \chidiv{\customcal{D}^\star}{\customcal{D}}= 
            {\int \inparen{\nfrac{{\rm d} \customcal{D}^\star(x)}{{\rm d} \customcal{D}(x)}}^2 {\rm d} \customcal{D}(x)} - 1$,
        the above is the same as 
        \[
            \customcal{D}^\star(S) \leq \customcal{D}(S)^{1/2}\cdot 
                \inparen{\chidiv{\customcal{D}^\star}{\customcal{D}}+1}^{1/2}
                \leq 
                    \sqrt{1+B}\cdot 
                    \customcal{D}(S)^{1/2}
                \,.
        \]
        The result follows since this holds for all measurable sets $S$.

nodes.name: KL transfer inequality
nodes.statement:
Let $\customcal{P}$ and $\customcal{Q}$ be probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and assume $\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}} < \infty$. 
            Then, for any measurable set $S$,
            \[
                \customcal{Q}(S) \;\le\; 
                \inf_{t>1} \Bigl\{t\,P(S) \;+\; \frac{\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}}{\ln t}\Bigr\}\,.
            \]

assumptions: Let $\customcal{P}$ and $\customcal{Q}$ be probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and assume $\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}} < \infty$.
conclusions: for any measurable set $S$,
nodes.label: lem:kl_transfer

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem E.3
nodes.statement:
First, \cref{lem:kl_transfer} implies that
            \[
            \customcal{D}^\star(S)\le\inf_{t>1}\Bigl\{t\,\customcal{D}(S)+\frac{C}{\ln t}\Bigr\}\,.
            \]
            Choosing $t=\nfrac{1}{\sqrt{\customcal{D}(S)}}$ and using that $\sqrt{z}\leq \frac{1}{\ln(1/z)}$ for all $z>0$, gives
            \[
            \customcal{D}^\star(S)\le\sqrt{\customcal{D}(S)}+\frac{2C}{\ln(1/\customcal{D}(S))}\le\frac{3\max\inbrace{1, C}}{\ln(1/\customcal{D}(S))}\,.
            \]
            which is equivalent to 
            \[
                \customcal{D}(S)\geq \exp\Bigl(-\frac{3 \max\inbrace{1, C}}{\customcal{D}^\star(S)}\Bigr)\,,
            \]
            that satisfies \textup{\tagform@{\ref{eq:mostGeneral:smoothness}}} with $r(m)=\exp(\nfrac{-3\max\inbrace{1, C}}{m})$ and $\lim_{m\to0^+}r(m)=0$.
nodes.section: E.5 Satisfying 3.1 via Bounds on KL-Divergence
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma E.4 with t = D(S)^{-1/2} and invert.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma E.4
nodes.statement:
Fix any $t>1$, and define the set
        \[
        T_t \;=\; \Bigl\{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \;>\; t \Bigr\}.
        \]
        On $T_t$, we have $\ln\inparen{\sfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}} > \ln t$. Hence,
        \[
        \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}} \;=\; \int \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;\ge\; \int_{T_t} \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;>\; (\ln t)\,Q(T_t)\,,
        \]
        which gives $Q(T_t) \le \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}/\ln t$. Next, split
        \[
        Q(S) \;=\; Q(S \cap T_t) \;+\; Q(S \cap T_t^c)\,.
        \]
        On $S \cap T_t^c$, we have $\nfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \le t$, so
        \[
        Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;=\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} \customcal{Q}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;\le\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} t\,\customcal{P}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;=\; t\,P(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
        Therefore,
        \[
        Q(S) \;\le\; Q(S \cap T_t) + Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; Q(T_t) + t\,P(S)
        \;\le\;
        \frac{\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}}{\ln t} + t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
        Since $t>1$ was arbitrary, taking the infimum over $t>1$ completes the proof.
nodes.section: E.5 Satisfying 3.1 via Bounds on KL-Divergence
nodes.statement_short: Split S by the likelihood-ratio level set T_t; bound Q(T_t) by KL/ln t and the rest by t P(S).

nodes.name: Level set T_t
nodes.statement:
Fix any $t>1$, and define the set
        \[
        T_t \;=\; \Bigl\{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \;>\; t \Bigr\}.
        \]
nodes.section: E.5 Satisfying 3.1 via Bounds on KL-Divergence

nodes.name: Q(T_t) at most KL / ln t
nodes.statement:
On $T_t$, we have $\ln\inparen{\sfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}} > \ln t$. Hence,
        \[
        \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}} \;=\; \int \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;\ge\; \int_{T_t} \customcal{Q}(x)\,\ln{\frac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)}}\,{\rm d} x
        \;>\; (\ln t)\,Q(T_t)\,,
        \]
        which gives $Q(T_t) \le \kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}/\ln t$.
nodes.section: E.5 Satisfying 3.1 via Bounds on KL-Divergence

nodes.name: Bound on the complement
nodes.statement:
Next, split
        \[
        Q(S) \;=\; Q(S \cap T_t) \;+\; Q(S \cap T_t^c)\,.
        \]
        On $S \cap T_t^c$, we have $\nfrac{\customcal{Q}(x)}{\customcal{P}(x)} \le t$, so
        \[
        Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;=\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} \customcal{Q}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;\le\; \int_{S \cap T_t^c} t\,\customcal{P}(x)\,{\rm d} x
        \;=\; t\,P(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
nodes.section: E.5 Satisfying 3.1 via Bounds on KL-Divergence

nodes.name: Combine and take infimum
nodes.statement:
Therefore,
        \[
        Q(S) \;\le\; Q(S \cap T_t) + Q(S \cap T_t^c)
        \;\le\; Q(T_t) + t\,P(S)
        \;\le\;
        \frac{\kl{\customcal{Q}}{\customcal{P}}}{\ln t} + t\,P(S)\,.
        \]
        Since $t>1$ was arbitrary, taking the infimum over $t>1$ completes the proof.

nodes.name: Adversarially Corrupted Gaussian Source
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Example (Adversarially Corrupted Gaussian Source):}\quad
                Suppose that $\customcal{D}^\star$ is a Gaussian distribution $\customcal{N}(\mu^\star,\Sigma^\star)$.
                Consider a data source that is $(1-\gamma)$-corrupted (for some $\gamma\in (0,1]$):
                    with probability $\gamma$, the source outputs a sample from $\customcal{D}^\star$, and, otherwise, outputs an arbitrary sample that may depend on the past samples and the knowledge of the learning algorithm.

nodes.statement_short: A source returning a Gaussian sample with probability gamma and an adversarial sample otherwise.

nodes.statement: We show that one can efficiently convert the above $(1-\gamma)$-corrupted source for any $\gamma>0$, into one satisfying the requirements of the List Decoding PIU Model with $\ell= \mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{1}{\gamma})$.

conclusions: one can efficiently convert the above $(1-\gamma)$-corrupted source for any $\gamma>0$, into one satisfying the requirements of the List Decoding PIU Model with $\ell= \mathrm{poly}(\nfrac{1}{\gamma})$

nodes.name: Assumptions on the exponential family (appendix)
nodes.statement:
There is a subset $\Theta$ of the natural parameter space and $\Lambda\geq \lambda > 0$ and $\eta>0$ such that:
                \begin{enumerate}
                    \item \textbf{(Interiority)}           
                        $\theta^\star$ is in the $\eta$-relative-interior $\Theta(\eta)$ of $\Theta$.
                    \item \textbf{(Projection Oracle)} There is an efficient projection oracle to the $\eta$-relative-interior of $\Theta$.
                    \item \textbf{(Bounded Fisher-Information)} For any $\theta\in \Theta$,
                    $\lambda I \preceq \ensuremath{\operatornamewithlimits{\rm Cov}}_{x\sim \customcal{E}(\theta)}[t(x)]\preceq \Lambda I$.
                \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Negative log-likelihoods
nodes.statement:
Fix $\beta= \nfrac{1}{2}$. 
                Let the (corrupted) samples be $X=\inbrace{x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n}$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_{r}$ be the set of \textit{uncorrupted} samples from $X$.
                For each $i$, define $f_i\colon \mathbb{R}^m\to \mathbb{R}^m$ to be the negative log-likelihood function, \textit{i.e.}{}, 
                $f_i(\theta) \coloneqq -\log\inparen{\customcal{E}(x_i; \theta)}$.
                Let $\overline{f}\colon \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^m$ be the population log-likelihood, \textit{i.e.}{}, $\overline{f}(\theta)=\operatornamewithlimits{\mathbb{E}}_{z\sim \customcal{E}(\theta^\star)}\insquare{-\log\inparen{z;\theta}}$.
nodes.section: E.6 Generating List of Distributions From Adversarially Corrupted Sources

nodes.name: Gradients and Hessians
nodes.statement:
Standard properties of the exponential density (see, \textit{e.g.}{}, \citet{dasgupta2008asymptotic}) imply that:
                for all $i$ and $\theta$
                \begin{align*}
                    \boldsymbol\NABLA f_i(\theta) &= \boldsymbol\NABLA A(\theta) - t(x_i)
                    ~~\quad\quadtext{and}~~
                    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 f_i(\theta) = \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 A(\theta)\,,\\
                    \boldsymbol\NABLA \overline{f}(\theta) &= \boldsymbol\NABLA A(\theta) - \boldsymbol\NABLA A(\theta^\star)
                    \quadtext{and}~~
                    \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 \overline{f}(\theta) = \boldsymbol\NABLA^2 A(\theta)\,.
                \end{align*}
                Where $A\colon \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is the log-partition function of the exponential family and $t\colon \mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}^m$ is the sufficient statistic of the exponential family.
nodes.section: E.6 Generating List of Distributions From Adversarially Corrupted Sources

nodes.name: Strong convexity
nodes.statement:
